About this site

How it works, what's covered, what isn't yet.

What this is

The league's record book and reference shelf, rebuilt from Yahoo's data for every season since 2012 and refreshed as games finish. It turns the analysis Mike has done by hand for years (luck, records, keeper streaks, playoff history) into pages that keep themselves current.

What's in it

Commentary & League Info: Mike's writeups, the rules, and how they got that way.
Standings & Records: this season, all time, champions, the record book, playoffs.
Manager Resources: luck, over and under achievers, positional strength, player search.
Draft & Keepers and Transactions: every draft, keeper, trade and FAAB bid on Yahoo.
Teams: one page per manager.

Known gaps

Yahoo's history starts in 2010, and 2010 and 2011 are not loaded yet; 2006 to 2011 champions and records will come from Mike's records. Off-season trades and future picks that were never entered in Yahoo do not appear yet. Season player points count only the weeks a player was on a roster in this league.

League rules

Current rules, with the open questions up top.

Open questions for the league

These rules are written down more than one way. Every version is listed with its source. They are for the league to settle; none is marked as correct here.

How big is the fine for not starting a full lineup?
Version A: The fine climbs 15, 30, 45, 60 FAAB and keeps going, per empty slot. If you run out of FAAB, it rolls into future years. Source: League Doc, Rules tab
Version B: Per empty slot, 15, 30, 45, then 45 for each one after that. Source: League Doc, 2023 summit topics
Version C: Per empty slot, rising 15 per violation, capped at 45. Source: Substack, "2023 Summit Results"
Do missed field goals from 40 to 49 yards cost a point, and since when?
Version A: Misses from 0 to 39 yards are -1. Misses of 40+ cost nothing. Source: Yahoo league settings, 2026 season (this is what actually scored)
Version B: All misses under 50 yards are -1. Source: League Doc, Rules tab (kicker scoring from 2022)
Version C: Passed: add -1 for misses from 40 to 49 yards. No start season recorded. Source: 2025 summit (League Doc topics and Substack "Rules Summit Results")

League basics

Twelve teams, keeper league, on Yahoo since 2010 (the league itself dates to 2006).

Buy-in is $50 per team, paid before the draft. The pot pays the champion 80% and the runner-up 20%. Teams may opt out, but once in they stay in. An opted-out team cannot be paid; if one finishes in the money, the next team down takes that prize. (Adopted at the 2024 summit, 6 to 4.)

Roster

SlotCount
QB1
WR3
RB2
TE1
K1
DEF1
Bench6
IR1

No flex. In 2020 only, the league added a seventh bench spot for COVID, which is why the 2020 draft ran 16 rounds.

You must start an active player in every slot, every week, including after you are eliminated. A player on bye or injured does not count as active. See the open question on the penalty amount below. If the team that would be fined wins that matchup, the fine is waived.

Keepers

Each team may keep up to 6 players. Keepers can be any players on your roster at the end of the prior season, or players you traded for in the off-season.

Keepers fill your last 6 draft slots, normally Rounds 10 to 15. Keeper slots are tradeable, so a team can hold more or fewer than 6 in a given year.

Keepers are declared in Yahoo by the keeper deadline, usually a week before the draft. A pre-keeper trade deadline falls about 24 hours earlier. After the keeper deadline, anyone not kept goes back into the draft pool and cannot be traded.

Draft

Draft order for Rounds 1 and 2 comes from a lottery among the six non-playoff teams. Current odds of the #1 pick:

FinishOdds of #1 pick
12th25%
11th25%
10th15%
9th15%
8th10%
7th10%

Starting with the 2027 draft, all six non-playoff teams get equal odds (16.667%). Adopted at the 2025 summit.

Playoff teams pick by the round they were eliminated, with regular-season standing as the tiebreaker. Rounds 3 to 15: lottery teams pick in reverse regular-season order; playoff teams keep their Round 1 order.

Each pick has a 60-second clock.

Trades

Trades process immediately; there is no review period.

Trades may include any rostered player and any draft pick a team controls, with no limit on how far ahead. Conditions may be attached to picks (for example, a 1st becomes a 2nd if the player misses a set number of games).

Picks already tied up in a conditional trade can be traded again, but only with an agreed backup pick in case the condition goes the other way. Deals cannot be renegotiated later.

No player-to-be-named-later. Only picks and FAAB can move as part of a condition.

Trade back rule: if you trade a player away, you cannot reacquire him by trade for the rest of that season and the following season (seasons end at the Championship). He can be reacquired sooner if he passes through waivers or the draft.

Trade moratorium: from 10pm on the Wednesday after Thanksgiving until the Championship ends. (Moved one week later at the 2023 summit, effective 2024.)

Waivers

FAAB waivers with 2-day claims. The waiver tiebreaker is a weekly rolling list: the last-place team gets top priority only on the first claim of the week (2020 summit). Players can be added straight to IR (2020 summit).

Schedule and playoffs

14-week regular season since 2021 (13 weeks before that).

Six teams make the playoffs. The top two seeds get a Round 1 bye. The bracket is reseeded before the semifinals. Round 1 is Week 15.

Scoring

Non-PPR. Passing: 1 point per 25 yards, 6 per TD, -2 per INT. Rushing and receiving: 1 point per 10 yards, 6 per TD. Two-point conversions 2. Every fumble is -2, even if recovered by the offense.

Kickers score by distance since 2022: 0.1 point per yard of a made field goal, 1 per extra point made, -1 per extra point missed. Missed field goals: see the open question below.

Defense: sack 1, interception 2, fumble recovery 1, TD 6, safety 2, blocked kick 3, 4th-down stop 1, tackle for loss 0.5, three-and-out forced 0.5, plus points-allowed and yards-allowed tiers.

Summits

To put a topic on the summit agenda, five managers must agree to discuss it. Agreeing to discuss is not agreeing to the change.

FPOR value board

Fantasy points over replacement for every pick, keeper and pickup, against what the draft slot usually returns.

How to read this board

FPOR (fantasy points over replacement) is points scored minus what a freely available player at the same position would have scored over the same weeks. Replacement is the Nth-best per-game scorer among rostered players: QB 15, RB 30, WR 42, TE 14, K 13, DEF 13 (WG starts QB, 2 RB, 3 WR, TE, K, DEF with no flex).

The price line. WG has no auction prices, so a pick's price is where it was taken. The dashed line is the FPOR an average pick at that slot has produced this season (rounds 1 to 9). Cards are shaded by how far each player sits above (blue) or below (red) the line, in standard deviations. Keepers and pickups have no pick price, so each is shaded against its own group's average.

Counting. Drafted players and keepers count every week on a roster in this league (weeks parked on IR are skipped); pickups count only the run of weeks on the team that claimed them. Only the top 36 pickups by FPOR get cards.

Ported from the I Yearn value board. Points are Yahoo league scoring.

All 12 teams, winning bids only.

FPOR per $ is fantasy points over replacement the claimed players produced for that manager, divided by FAAB spent; managers under $10 are not ranked. Overpay is the gap between a winning bid and the next-best real offer (claims nobody else bid on count as $0 over). "Since pickup" counts only the run of weeks the player stayed on the claiming team. Winning bids come from the Yahoo API; losing offers from Yahoo's FAB Offers page for every season, read Nov 9, 2026. Free-agent adds (no waiver period) are not claims; see the transaction log.
